subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit raw-stream disable from launchd/process env override durable generated service-env or state-dir `.env` enables for macOS LaunchAgents, and should doctor/service repair remove stale raw-stream entries?
rationale: Both outcomes affect compatibility and sensitive logging: preserving durable service env may surprise operators trying to stop private stream logs, while making `0`/unset authoritative may change setups that intentionally enabled raw-stream through generated service env or config.

options.title: Make explicit disable authoritative
options.body: Treat false-like process or launchd values as a hard disable, repair stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document the cleanup path.

options.title: Keep durable enable precedence
options.body: Leave generated service-env and state-dir `.env` as durable enables, but document that operators must remove those entries or run a repair path to disable logging.

options.title: Require a doctor-managed migration
options.body: Pause the runtime change until `openclaw doctor --fix` owns detection and removal of stale raw-stream LaunchAgent env state.

recommendation.title: Make explicit disable authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat false-like process or launchd values as a hard disable, repair stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document the cleanup path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest cross-surface history match for raw-stream runtime and service/env helper work in the affected paths.
